entries.title: Library topics take in more of your articles
entries.body: The topics above your library file an article under subjects it deals with in substance, not only its main one, and a narrower topic can include articles from outside the broader topic it sits under. This arrives gradually, as each set of topics is next reconsidered and as you add articles.

entries.title: Quick search lets more passages through
entries.body: Quick results in Search accept passages that match your words a little less closely than before, so searches generally show more. Some show fewer: where a search used to find nothing close and fell back to a list of looser matches, one closer match now takes the place of that list.

entries.title: Bottom bar: modes reordered, Help link removed
entries.body: On the bar of modes under an article, Glossary now comes before FAQ and Citations before Referee. The Help link has left the bar to make it less crowded; you can still reach Help from the command bar and from a mode's (i). If you are reading an article that is not yours, Help stays on the bar.

entries.title: Citations can match raised reference numbers
entries.body: Some papers cite with small raised numbers rather than numbers in brackets, and their reference-list entries were being lost. Citations can now match those numbers to the list. It judges by pattern, so it can sometimes be wrong. It applies when Citations is generated or regenerated for an article; results already saved are not rebuilt.

entries.title: A misread page of PDF endnotes is recovered
entries.body: In a PDF, a continuation page of endnotes could be read as ordinary paragraphs, so the note numbers pointing at it stayed plain digits rather than links. Such a page can now be recognised as notes when it follows a notes page. This applies only to PDFs added, or read in again, from now on; existing articles are unchanged.

entries.title: Help says when Summary offers a rewrite
entries.body: The Help page now says that a summary is written once and kept, and that Write it again appears only when the article has changed or you have changed your profile. Only the Help text changed; Summary behaves as it did.

entries.title: An unsent Chat question survives switching modes
entries.body: A question typed in Chat but not sent used to vanish when you switched to another mode. It is now still in the box when you come back, and the same goes for Remember's answer boxes and the floating chat window. It is not kept if you reload the page or close the tab.

entries.title: Unusual DOIs link to the right paper
entries.body: A DOI is the permanent identifier many papers carry. When one contained certain characters, such as a backslash, the link the app built from it could point to a different work. Those links, in Citations, in Debate and on pages for papers you have not read, are now built correctly. Links already saved are not rewritten.
